trust_decision.summary: Whether a context entry in a namespaced Policy may read a ConfigMap from a namespace other than the policy's own; at the pinned commit the ConfigMap loader resolves any substituted namespace (empty means 'default') without comparing it with the policy namespace, unlike the apiCall loader, which does.

landing_point.why: The advisory names ConfigMap context entries and the earlier apiCall fix; this is the only place where configMap.namespace is substituted and passed to resolver.Get.

fix_sites.entry_point: Namespaced kyverno.io Policy with a configMap context entry, evaluated by the admission webhook (validate/mutate/verifyImages) and by the background/report controllers through engine.ContextLoader (pkg/engine/engine.go:164-178)
Public API factories.DefaultContextLoaderFactory, used by cmd/internal/engine.go:52 for all controllers

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both changed sites are in the engine context-loading path the advisory points at; the factory change only passes policyNamespace through (pkg/engine/factories/contextloaderfactory.go:109).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the cleanup controller route: 'CleanupPolicy is a separate feature, its validation already forbids ConfigMap context entries (api/kyverno/v2/cleanup_policy_types.go:265-266), and apiCall was the subject of the earlier CVE, so neither belongs to this ConfigMap report.'

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: ClusterPolicies (policyNamespace == "") must still read ConfigMaps from any namespace, with an empty namespace defaulting to 'default'; namespaced Policies must still read same-namespace ConfigMaps, and an empty namespace now defaults to the policy namespace. Blocking all configMap entries, or defaulting to 'default' for namespaced policies, breaks legitimate policies.

O6_input_shapes: literal configMap.namespace different from the policy namespace (fix.diff:79-81)
variable-substituted namespace such as '{{ targetNs }}' resolving to another namespace (fix.diff:58, 79; test fix.diff:208-217)
non-string substitution result for namespace or name, previously an unchecked type assertion (fix.diff:54-57, 64-67)

O7_producer.where: policyNamespace is derived from the policy in the factory closure (pkg/engine/factories/contextloaderfactory.go:21-25); callers that pass a nil policy (pkg/controllers/cleanup/controller.go:173-174) get an empty value, which the loaders treat as a cluster-wide policy.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A namespaced CleanupPolicy's spec.context is loaded through DefaultContextLoaderFactory with a nil policy, so policyNamespace is "" and both the apiCall namespace check and the new ConfigMap check are skipped for a namespace-scoped CRD.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Cleanup is a separate controller and feature; ConfigMap context entries are forbidden for cleanup policies at validation time (api/kyverno/v2/cleanup_policy_types.go:261-269), so the route reaches the apiCall sink (earlier CVE), not the ConfigMap sink from this report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: pkg/controllers/cleanup, 2 package hops from pkg/engine/context/loaders; the CRD is namespaced (config/crds/kyverno/kyverno.io_cleanuppolicies.yaml:19)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A namespaced Policy's globalReference context entry reads any cluster-scoped GlobalContextEntry (which may cache resources from other namespaces); the gctx loader takes no policyNamespace.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: GlobalContextEntries are cluster-scoped, admin-curated shared caches, meant to be readable by every policy by design.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same factory file; the loader is in pkg/engine/context/loaders/globalcontext.go:97-103

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A namespaced Policy's verifyImages attestor keys.secret may name a Secret in any namespace, and that Secret is resolved via a k8s:// key reference without any comparison with the policy namespace.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It holds only a public verification key, never enters the JSON context, and is image verification rather than context loading.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: pkg/engine/internal, a different package and feature from the context loaders

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An imageRegistry context entry's imageRegistryCredentials secrets resolved from a namespace taken from the entry instead of the policy namespace.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The loaders take a namespace-free constructor, as NewConfigMapLoader did before the fix; a maintainer adding namespace-qualified credential references would copy that signature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second ConfigMap-backed loader (for example in a CLI or test-store resolver path) built without the policyNamespace argument.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: There is a separate CLI store context loader wrapping the factory (cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/store/contextloader.go:13-43); a parallel implementation that skips the new parameter is plausible.

O9_family: authorization / tenant isolation (CWE-863 incorrect authorization: cross-namespace read via a privileged controller)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.26.x (per recent commit dc9dc4593), go modules
O10_build.project_tests: Unit tests with mock resolvers: pkg/engine/apicall/apiCall_test.go (namespace checks at :337, :389), pkg/engine/factories/factories_test.go; the fix adds pkg/engine/context/loaders/configmap_test.go (fix.diff:98-246). No cluster is needed for loader-level tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the namespace comparison in configmap.go for literal namespaces only, keep defaulting an empty namespace to 'default', and leave the nil-policy cleanup controller call unchanged.

out_of_scope_notes: The CEL library context provider's GetResource/ListResources (pkg/cel/libs/context.go:134-162) take any namespace without a policy-namespace check; it is a different engine, and I did not check whether namespaced CEL policy kinds exist at this commit.

kubectl-kyverno apply evaluates CleanupPolicies with DefaultContextLoaderFactory(nil) and a nil policy (cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/apply/command.go:843, 868); this is a local CLI, not a trust boundary.
